evals.prompt: Use $rrm-brand-strategy-specialist to create the canonical brand guide from a flight school repo with program pages, FAQs, reviews, financing content, and location pages.
evals.expected_output: A sourced .agents/right-rudder-marketing/shared/outputs/brand-guide.md with UVP, ICP, personas, offers, objections, proof points, risky claims, voice, conversion paths, and evergreen blog opportunities.
expectations: Scans repo content before asking questions
Creates or updates the canonical brand-guide.md artifact
Includes source paths for concrete claims
Separates safe claims from risky claims
Creates behavior-based ICPs
Identifies durable blog opportunities grounded in client positioning

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-brand-strategy-specialist when .agents/right-rudder-marketing/shared/outputs/brand-guide.md already exists and the reviewed source material has no material changes.
evals.expected_output: A no-update-needed response that lists the reviewed sources and explains that the existing brand guide remains current.
expectations: Does not rewrite the guide for style
Compares source inventory against the existing guide
Reports no update needed
Does not create a tactical blog brief

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-brand-strategy-specialist when a flight school has changed pricing, program inclusions, and proof claims since the existing brand guide was created.
evals.expected_output: An updated brand-guide.md with update notes describing the pricing, program, and proof changes, while preserving sourced claims and risky-claim cautions.
expectations: Updates only materially affected guide sections
Preserves source paths for concrete claims
Adds update notes with reasons
Flags aviation claims needing rrm-aviation-industry-expert review
Does not create a per-post blog brief by default

evals.prompt: The site has thin content and no clear proof points. Build what you can and tell me what is missing.
evals.expected_output: A partial brand guide plus a concise list of high-impact missing questions.
expectations: Does not invent proof
Labels inferences clearly
Asks only strategic questions
Still produces a usable partial guide

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-brand-strategy-specialist to build the canonical brand guide from a flight school repo with program pages, testimonials, homepage copy, and interview notes that reveal how students talk about the school.
evals.expected_output: A sourced brand guide that includes the usual strategy sections plus a company voice sourcebook with company POV, reusable phrases, testimonial language worth echoing, aviation moments, reader aspiration and fear, safe excitement boundaries, and banned robotic phrases.
expectations: Extracts voice from client-owned copy and testimonials instead of inventing tone adjectives
Captures phrases that sound like the company
Captures company-seat rewrites for fleet, simulator, airport, instructor, financing, and student-story language
Captures aviation scenes future blogs can reuse
Captures reader aspirations and fears
Defines safe excitement boundaries
Lists robotic, source-audit, and outside-reviewer phrases to avoid in future blog posts
Defines natural confirmation phrasing for current details that may change
Preserves source paths for all concrete claims

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-brand-strategy-specialist to build the canonical brand guide from a flight school repo with existing blog frontmatter, staff bios, an about page, and client notes that identify one named author with military background plus some team-authored posts.
evals.expected_output: A sourced brand guide with an Author Voice And Byline Strategy section that distinguishes team voice from named-author voice, records author evidence, permits only light sourced persona cues, and defines team fallback voice when no author bio exists.
expectations: Inspects existing blog author fields, author images, staff bios, about pages, and extra-information notes
Identifies whether the durable byline mode is team or named-author
Records source-backed author role, credentials, and aviation background when available
Defines permitted persona cues without encouraging heavy first-person writing
Says to keep a named author credit but fall back to team voice when no usable bio exists
Flags invented author credentials, service history, airline experience, and personal anecdotes as off-limits
Treats author/byline changes as material voice changes
